name: Brazilian butt lift

card.summary: Autologous fat transfer to the buttocks; powerful, well-documented results in surgical reviews, and a procedure with documented deaths that has driven safety changes.
card.aka: BBL, gluteal fat grafting, buttock lipoinjection
card.note: Surgical literature reports deaths from gluteal lipoinjection; safety technique and anatomy are a central focus of the field.

quick.overview:
A Brazilian butt lift takes fat from elsewhere on the body by liposuction and injects it into the buttocks to add volume and reshape the silhouette. It is discussed in looksmaxxing forums mainly as a female-appearance procedure and as an analogue for male body contouring.

Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing body contouring operation, delivering results other procedures can not match, alongside a strong emphasis on safety and anatomy.
quick.mechanism: Fat is harvested, processed and injected into the buttock tissue. Some of the transferred fat is reabsorbed, so volume can change over the following months and repeat sessions are sometimes used. Ultrasound guidance is described by some surgeons as a way to visualise the injection plane.
quick.risks: Complications reported in the literature include fat resorption, asymmetry, infection, seroma and persistent numbness. A 2015 report from Mexican surgeons recorded 13 deaths from gluteal lipoinjection, and a 2019 meta-analysis reported complication rates of 7% for fat grafting versus 31% for implants. It is an Rx surgical procedure, and cosmetic tourism for it is a subject of media coverage.

lead: Brazilian butt lift (BBL) is the common name for buttock augmentation using fat transfer, in which a patient's own fat is harvested by liposuction and injected into the gluteal region [1][2]. People have it to add volume and projection to the buttocks and to reshape the whole silhouette, since the liposuction step also thins areas such as the abdomen, flanks or thighs, which can make the waist-to-hip contour look more pronounced [3][4][6].

Wikipedia notes that the term probably comes from the Brazilian surgeon Ivo Pitanguy, who pioneered related surgery in the 1960s, while the Venezuelan surgeon Eduardo Krulig described buttock lipoinjection in 1987; popularity rose sharply in the 2010s and 2020s, which Wikipedia attributes to social media trends [2][10][11].

Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing procedure in body contouring and a large share of the recent literature focuses on safety, anatomy and technique [1][3][4]. A 2015 report documented deaths from gluteal lipoinjection among Mexican surgeons, a 2019 meta-analysis put the complication rate for fat grafting at 7% against 31% for implants, and a 2018 review stated that fat grafting appears to carry a mortality rate significantly higher than other aesthetic procedures [2][12].

In looksmaxxing forums the procedure is mostly discussed in terms of female appearance, with some users asking about male equivalents and others debating what drives the body shapes seen in public [5][16]. UK news coverage reported on advertising rulings and parliamentary calls for tighter regulation of the industry [14][15].

paras: Buttock augmentation covers several operations. Gluteal implants are placed under the gluteus maximus muscle through a midline incision, with tissues taking about six to eight months to settle and four to six weeks of convalescence. Lipoinjection harvests fat from the abdomen, flanks or thighs and injects it into the buttocks. Body contouring approaches combine dermal-fat flap surgery with liposculpture, often for patients after massive weight loss. Reduction procedures use liposuction, including ultrasonic-assisted techniques, to remove volume instead [10].

The BBL is the lipoinjection form. Gluteal augmentation by autologous fat transfer is described in surgical texts as a way to transform the body silhouette, with proper patient selection, planning and technique said to be critical to safety and results [6]. Because liposuction is part of the operation, ultrasound-assisted lipoplasty has been reviewed as one of the technologies used in body contouring [17].

Wikipedia says the name 'Brazilian butt lift' is thought to come from Ivo Pitanguy, who pioneered the surgery in the 1960s [10]. Pitanguy (1926-2016) was a Brazilian plastic surgeon based in Rio de Janeiro who founded a clinic that drew surgeons from around the world and trained thousands of surgeons; after the 1961 Niteroi circus fire he and his team treated hundreds of burn victims [11]. Wikipedia describes him as thought to be the creator of the Brazilian butt lift [11].

The Venezuelan plastic surgeon Eduardo Krulig described fat-injection techniques in 1987 and first used the term 'lipoinjection' [2][10]. The 2010s and 2020s brought a sharp rise in demand that the encyclopedia attributes to social media trends [2].

By the 2010s, surgical societies and journals were publishing dedicated work on safety. A 2018 series in Clinics in Plastic Surgery covered anatomy, evaluation systems and complications of gluteal augmentation [7][12][13], and a 2023 series returned to safety, ultrasound guidance and full-body harmony [1][3][9].

Anatomy-focused reviews emphasise the clinically relevant structures to avoid complications and to improve patient satisfaction [7]. A classification system for gluteal evaluation was developed because rising patient demand required a more structured approach to assessing buttock anatomy and planning procedures [13].

Surgeons writing in 2023 describe the buttock as a feature that has to harmonise with the rest of the body to look attractive, and describe the gluteal framework concept and new infiltration techniques intended to give more natural results [3]. An assessment tool for optimising BBL results has also been published [9].

Fat is harvested by liposuction, processed and injected into the buttock tissue. Some of the transferred fat is reabsorbed, so volume can change over the following months, and repeat sessions are sometimes used [10]. Surgeons have published on ultrasound-guided fat grafting, which allows the operator to see the subcutaneous space during injection [8]. Recovery involves compression garments and activity restriction, and the final contour generally appears at six to twelve months depending on healing [2][10].

Reviews describe powerful and consistent results when the operation is carried out with careful planning [6]. The 2023 safety review describes gluteal fat grafting as delivering results that no other procedure can achieve [1]. Wikipedia notes that some transferred fat may be reabsorbed and repeat sessions may be needed [2]. An experience of over 3,000 patients and an assessment tool for optimising results have been described in the literature [8][9].

Evidence consists mainly of surgeon case series, reviews and technique papers. A report of experience with more than 3,000 patients was published in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery, and a separate paper introduced a BBL assessment tool [8][9].

A 2019 meta-analysis of 46 publications cited by Wikipedia found a complication rate of 7% for fat grafting versus 31% for implants [2]. No randomized trial of BBL compared with no surgery was identified.

Wikipedia reports that a study of 413 Mexican plastic surgeons documented 64 liposuction-related deaths, 13 of them from gluteal lipoinjection, plus nine deaths in Colombia [2][10]. Other complications of fat injection include fat resorption, asymmetry, abscess, cellulitis and persistent numbness that can take up to two years to resolve [2][10].

A 2018 review of complications in gluteal augmentation says that autologous fat grafting seems to carry a mortality rate significantly higher than other aesthetic procedures, that implant-based augmentation is also difficult, and that societies and surgeons were developing guidelines based on theoretical causes [12]. For implants, listed risks include infection, wound dehiscence, rupture, seroma, capsular contracture and sciatic nerve injury; other reported dangers include lymphoedema after liquid silicone injection, thromboembolism and implant displacement [2][10].
A Clinics in Plastic Surgery review on safety in gluteal augmentation describes efforts made to improve the safety of the procedure [1].

UK news coverage reposted on aggregator sites carries headlines about the Advertising Standards Authority banning BBL adverts that used time-limited deals which, in the regulator's words, 'irresponsibly pressurise' customers, and about MPs describing the industry as a 'wild west' and urging a crackdown [14][15]. A television documentary on surgery complications was also covered under the title 'Botched: The Brazilian Butt Lift Nightmare' [18].

The wider subject of buttock aesthetics appears in popular science writing; a Wired excerpt shared on Lemmy discusses how surgeons once thought attractive buttock proportions should follow the Fibonacci sequence [19].

One looksmax.org thread reproduces a list of male analogues of BBL and breast implants, including pectoral implants and male buttock augmentation by fat or implant; another poster objected that height is not an equivalent [5]. A different thread asks whether women's larger buttocks reflect diet or surgery; replies attribute them to diet, training and clothing as well as to cosmetic surgery [16].

timeline.event: Ivo Pitanguy pioneers related buttock surgery in Brazil, per Wikipedia [10].
Pitanguy and his team treat hundreds of burn victims after the Niteroi circus fire, a case study in his career [11].
A report documents deaths from gluteal lipoinjection among Mexican surgeons [2].
A Clinics in Plastic Surgery series covers gluteal anatomy, classification and complications, including mortality [7][12][13].
A meta-analysis compares complication rates of fat grafting and implants [2].
A second Clinics in Plastic Surgery series addresses safety, body-contouring harmony and ultrasound-guided grafting [1][3][8].
A report of experience with over 3,000 BBL patients is published [8].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org BBL is raised mostly in discussion of female appearance and surgical equivalents for men. [5]

claims.claim: Men have BBL-style equivalents such as buttock augmentation
claims.believers: A post lists male buttock augmentation by fat or implant among analogues of BBL and breast implants. [5]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes buttock augmentation procedures generally, covering implants and lipoinjection, without sex-specific data. [2]

claims.claim: BBL is a high-impact, transformative surgery
claims.believers: The thread says it adds volume where there was little and reshapes sexually dimorphic features. [5]
claims.experts: Surgical reviews describe powerful results and also document deaths and complications. [1][2]

claims.claim: Women's larger buttocks seen today are partly due to BBLs.
claims.believers: Posters in a looksmax.org thread suggest that many women get BBLs and that surgery is respected as a looks upgrade [16].
claims.experts: Wikipedia attributes the rise in procedures in the 2010s and 2020s to social media trends; no study in the cited material compares surgery rates with other causes of body-shape change [2].

claims.claim: BBL carries unusually high risk compared with other cosmetic surgery.
claims.believers: Posters in a looksmax.org thread say people who get surgery are respected, and mock others who call it too risky [16].
claims.experts: A 2018 review states fat grafting appears to have a significantly higher mortality rate than other aesthetic procedures, and Mexican surgeons documented 13 deaths from gluteal lipoinjection [2][12].

claims.claim: Fat grafting is safer than implants.
claims.believers: Advocates of fat grafting generally cite the lower complication rate compared with implants, as reported in surgical literature [2].
claims.experts: A 2019 meta-analysis found fat grafts had a complication rate of about 7% against 31% for implants, although the same literature documents deaths from fat injection [2][12].

angle.text: A BBL moves volume from one area of the body to the buttocks, so the result is both added fullness at the back and a slimmer donor area. Surgeons describe the aim as harmony of the buttocks with the rest of the body contour [3][4].
